Whether a Shape-Constrained Term Is at the Vertex of Its Shape

Source: R/scs.R
term_vertex.Rd

Returns the names of the coefficients of the levels of a term whose constrained coordinates are all at their bound, and an empty vector when there are none.

Usage

term_vertex(term, coef = NULL, ...)

Arguments

term

A built term.

coef

The coefficients, one per coefficient of the term, or NULL for the coefficients that the term carries.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A character vector of coefficient names, with the attribute complete, TRUE when every level that carries a shape is at the vertex.

Details

Each coordinate that a shape constrains is \(b_j = l_j + g^{-1}(\gamma_j)\), with \(l_j\) its bound (zero, or a minimum slope). When the data go against the shape every \(b_j\) goes to its bound and every \(\gamma_j\) to \(-\infty\): the curve is the one at the bound (constant, linear for a plain curvature, or of slope min_slope) and the columns of the block on those coordinates vanish. A level is at the vertex when the derivative \((g^{-1})'(\gamma_j)\) of every constrained coordinate is below \(10^{-10}\) times its value at the default start: the inner fit stops somewhere on the way to \(-\infty\) (measured between -67 and -320), and a curve whose every constrained slope is that small is the curve at the bound to that accuracy. The base method returns an empty vector, which is right for a term without a shape.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(50))
tm <- term_build(scs(x, shape_increasing()), dd)
term_vertex(tm, coef = rep(-300, length(term_coef_names(tm))))
#> [1] "scs(x).g1" "scs(x).g2" "scs(x).g3" "scs(x).g4" "scs(x).g5" "scs(x).g6"
#> [7] "scs(x).g7" "scs(x).g8" "scs(x).g9"
#> attr(,"complete")
#> [1] TRUE
term_vertex(tm, coef = rep(0, length(term_coef_names(tm))))
#> character(0)
#> attr(,"complete")
#> [1] FALSE
